title: Provider-neutral typed semantic evidence for bounded narrative continuation
independentExamples: A nonce process followed by a declaratively supported causal outcome
A renamed nonce goal followed by a continuation that satisfies the declared goal
A cooperative nonce exchange contrasted with a provider-declared social conflict
A positive containment state contrasted with a provider-declared inverse state
outputTypes: selected candidate identifier or explicit UNKNOWN
preconditions: one to sixty-four validated narrative events
two to thirty-two uniquely identified candidate frames
each provider record declares a bounded signed score and optional allowlisted semantic family
invariants: provider identifiers, benchmark identifiers, row identifiers, candidate order, and exact strings never dispatch core behavior
unknown semantic families fall back to event support or signed contradiction rather than creating executable policy
negative evidence remains negative through bounded scoring
provider records remain defeasible and retain source references
source-local development calibration is adapter policy and not universal semantic truth
uncertaintySemantics: DEFEASIBLE only above the declared minimum margin; UNKNOWN for a tie or insufficient margin; UNPARSED for an invalid payload
proofBehavior: Returns the semantic family, signed value, weight, contribution, relation, match type, and source reference in the ordinary ranking trace
kbMigration: No package-schema migration. ATOMIC, ConceptNet, and world-relations expose optional semanticEvidence methods while their existing query interfaces remain compatible.
